conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: B labels supplied vs. unsupplied outcomes inline on every case-study card (color-coded 'AFTER — SUPPLIED OUTCOME' plus an italic 'not supplied' caveat) and repeats that framing right before the contact form, which more directly satisfies the job of deciding from evidence rather than self-description. B's form validation gives field-specific guidance wired to inputs via aria-describedby, while A only shows a generic repeated 'This field is required.' Most materially, A's submission confirmation claims 'Request sent. Mara will follow up directly about next steps' even though the build has no backend to send or guarantee anything, which is an unsupported claim; B's confirmation avoids that by only confirming what was locally recorded.
suspected_unblinding: B's sanitized source/evidence/ folder retained extra leftover iteration screenshots (desktop-1440-fixed.png, desktop-final.png, contact-error.png, contact-success.png, interactions-open.png, mobile-390.png) suggesting a multi-pass, screenshot-driven build process. That hints at a process difference between A and B but does not by itself indicate which team or treatment produced either output.

unsupported_claims.label: A
unsupported_claims.claim: Contact form success message states the request was sent and that Mara will follow up directly about next steps, but the build has no backend, so nothing is actually transmitted and no follow-up is guaranteed.

findings.label: A
findings.description: Submit confirmation asserts an outcome ('Request sent... Mara will follow up directly') that the static build cannot deliver, functioning as an unsupported commercial claim.
findings.evidence: A/source/app.js line 65: "Request sent. Mara will follow up directly about next steps."; no fetch/XHR call exists anywhere in A/source/app.js to back the claim.

findings.label: A
findings.description: Invalid form fields get aria-invalid but the visible error text is never linked to the input via aria-describedby, so a screen reader user is told a field is invalid without hearing why.
findings.evidence: A/source/app.js sets aria-invalid (line 31) but never references aria-describedby; A/source/index.html field-error paragraphs (e.g. line 182) have no id referenced by their input.

findings.label: A
findings.description: No persistent section navigation (Work/Process/Contact) is present, so the reviewer must scroll to find each part of the evidence within the stated 4-minute time budget.
findings.evidence: A/desktop.png shows only a title and hero CTA link, no nav bar; A/source/index.html has no <nav> landmark with anchor links (present in B/source/index.html).

findings.label: A
findings.description: The packet's evidence for the required 'Request a project conversation' interaction shows the untouched, empty default form rather than a submitted or validated state, so the required interaction is not visually demonstrated even though the underlying code supports it.
findings.evidence: A/evidence/interaction-03-request-project-conversation.png shows a blank form with no confirmation or error text.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The submit success message breaks the in-universe persuasive frame by addressing the museum director with developer/meta language about the build's implementation instead of staying diegetic.
findings.evidence: B/source/app.js line 132: "This build has no backend, so nothing was actually transmitted."

findings.label: B
findings.description: Contact form adds an Email field beyond the four fields the brief specifies (organization, project, timeline, budget range) — a minor unrequested scope addition.
findings.evidence: B/source/index.html line 251-253, field-email block with aria-describedby="hint-email".
